patient_overview.name: Lilia Galindo
patient_overview.description: Lilia Galindo is a 52-year-old Hispanic woman living in East Rutherford, New Jersey, in a crowded household of six, who comes in for a nutrition visit tied to her prediabetes, obesity, fibromyalgia and chronic low back pain. She answers questions in short, flat sentences and visibly wants the appointment to move along, warming up only slightly when asked something a second time. She does not believe anything is really wrong with how she eats and sees this visit as something she's being made to do rather than something she asked for. A dietitian meeting her will need patience, plain language, and a willingness to circle back to sensitive topics rather than push on the first try.

demographics.occupation: Not in the labor force; disabled from working due to chronic pain and fibromyalgia, previously worked as a laundromat attendant
demographics.residence: East Rutherford, New Jersey; household of 6
demographics.cultural_context: Lilia was raised in a working-class Hispanic household where big family meals mattered, but she has lived alone in terms of cooking for years inside a crowded house — everyone else in the household is on different schedules and eats separately. She never learned to cook for just herself and never saw the point in trying. Spanish is still her most comfortable language, and she prefers when health information is explained simply rather than with numbers and charts, which have never meant much to her.

medical_history: Past pregnancy history of miscarriage since 2020
Miscarriage in first trimester (2023-10 to 2023-11, resolved)
current_symptoms: Constant dull ache in the low back that flares with standing too long
Widespread muscle soreness and tender spots described as 'hurts everywhere some days'
Tired most of the day no matter how much she sleeps
Occasional lightheadedness she attributes to being 'just tired'
Trouble falling and staying asleep because of pain
clinical_findings: Obese body habitus with weight centered around the abdomen
Moves stiffly and slowly when rising from the chair, favoring her lower back
Pale conjunctiva and slightly pale nail beds consistent with low hemoglobin
Appears fatigued, rubs her lower back during the conversation

medications.name: Acetaminophen 325 MG Oral Tablet [Tylenol]
medications.frequency: As needed, roughly most days for pain
medications.adherence: Takes it when the pain gets bad; does not take it on a fixed schedule
medications.patient_concerns: Doesn't think it does much anymore, says she 'just takes it anyway'

supplements_and_otc: Topical menthol pain cream for her back

nutrition_profile.dietary_pattern: Relies heavily on microwave and frozen ready meals, canned soups, and fast food pickup; little fresh cooking
food_preferences: Pan dulce from the corner bakery
Fried chicken from the drive-through near her house
foods_or_behaviors_to_explore: Nighttime binge eating of chips or sweets when pain or stress is high
Skipping real meals then eating a large amount later
Frequency of fast food versus home-prepared food
Portion sizes with ready meals eaten straight from the container
nutrition_profile.meal_pattern: Irregular; often skips breakfast, grazes on snacks through the day, then eats a large meal late at night
nutrition_profile.hydration: Mostly soda and sweetened iced tea, little plain water
nutrition_profile.physical_activity: Very limited; walking is painful and she avoids it, mostly sits or lies down most of the day
nutrition_profile.substance_use: Never smoked; audit-C score 0, essentially does not drink alcohol
nutrition_profile.sleep: Poor, disrupted by pain, often up late which is when the heavier eating happens

psychosocial_profile.personality: Blunt, impatient, no-nonsense; wants answers fast and gets irritated by long explanations
psychosocial_profile.communication_style: Gives short, clipped answers at first; opens up a little more only if asked the same question again in a different way; dislikes being lectured
goals: Just wants her back to hurt less
Wants to be left alone about her weight
concerns: Being told she has to change everything about how she eats
Being judged for eating convenience food
beliefs: Thinks her weight and blood sugar numbers are 'not that bad' and not worth fussing over
Believes the pain is the real problem, not the food
Thinks diets never work for her so there's no point trying
motivations: Avoiding more doctor visits and more lectures
Keeping her partner from worrying so much
fears: Being told she needs to lose a lot of weight
Ending up unable to care for herself at all
barriers: Chronic pain makes cooking and standing in the kitchen hard
Cooking for one feels pointless in a house of six eating on different schedules
Low health literacy makes nutrition information confusing
No motivation to change because she doesn't see the problem
strengths: Has a partner who checks on her and cares
Keeps regular medical checkups even if reluctantly
psychosocial_profile.support_system: Lives with a partner who is supportive but anxious and hovers over her, frequently asking if she's eaten or taken her medicine, which Lilia says 'gets to be a lot'; also shares the house with other family members on different schedules
psychosocial_profile.readiness_to_change: Precontemplation; does not see her eating as a problem and resists the idea that it connects to her blood sugar or pain

initial_information: Says her back pain is the main issue, not her diet
Mentions she mostly eats frozen meals because cooking for the house doesn't make sense for just her
States she doesn't drink and never smoked
Says the doctor sent her here, not that she asked to come
discoverable_information: Admits she skips breakfast most days and eats most of her food late in the day
Says soda is easier than water because 'water doesn't do anything for me'
Mentions her partner keeps asking her if she's eaten, which annoys her a little
Describes her days as mostly sitting because standing hurts her back
reluctant_information: Eventually admits that on bad pain nights she'll eat a whole bag of chips or a sleeve of cookies without really noticing until it's gone
Admits she sometimes eats in her room alone so her partner won't see how much
hidden_information: Lilia has never told anyone, including her partner, that after her miscarriage in 2023 she started eating late at night to fall back asleep and never stopped
She throws away evidence of binge wrappers in a bag outside rather than the kitchen trash so her partner won't notice

opportunities.learning_objective: Practice motivational interviewing with a patient in precontemplation who denies any need to change.
expected_discoveries: Lilia does not connect her diet to her prediabetes or weight
She responds better to open-ended, low-pressure questions than direct advice
possible_patient_reactions: I don't see why this matters, my numbers aren't even that bad.
Everybody's gotta eat something, I don't know what you want me to say.

opportunities.learning_objective: Adapt nutrition education for low health literacy.
expected_discoveries: Lilia does not understand lab values or percentages
She responds to simple, concrete language and visual comparisons rather than numbers
possible_patient_reactions: I don't know what that A1C thing means, just tell me if it's bad or not.
Can you just say it simple?

opportunities.learning_objective: Explore comfort eating and shame around binge episodes using a non-judgmental approach.
expected_discoveries: Lilia eats large amounts of snack food at night when pain or stress is high
She hides evidence of binge eating from her partner
The behavior appears tied to unresolved grief from her 2023 miscarriage
possible_patient_reactions: Shuts down or changes subject if asked directly
I don't want to talk about that.
Eventually, quietly: 'It's not like I plan it, it just happens.'

opportunities.learning_objective: Address barriers to meal preparation in a crowded household with chronic pain.
expected_discoveries: Standing to cook aggravates her back and fibromyalgia pain
Cooking for herself alone in a house of six feels pointless to her
Reliance on ready meals and fast food is largely about convenience and energy conservation
possible_patient_reactions: Why cook a whole meal just for me?
Standing in the kitchen kills my back after five minutes.

opportunities.learning_objective: Involve a hovering but supportive partner appropriately in nutrition counseling.
expected_discoveries: Partner's constant checking feels like pressure to Lilia rather than help
There may be an opportunity to redirect partner support toward practical help, like grocery shopping, instead of monitoring
possible_patient_reactions: He means well but he's always asking if I ate, it's annoying.

opportunities.learning_objective: Discuss hydration and beverage choices in the context of prediabetes.
expected_discoveries: Soda and sweetened tea are her main fluids
She is unaware or dismissive of the link between sugary drinks and blood sugar
possible_patient_reactions: Water's boring, I don't like it.
One soda's not gonna kill me.

assumptions: Lilia's chronic pain and fibromyalgia significantly limit her mobility and willingness to cook
The 2023 miscarriage is treated as an emotional contributor to her nighttime comfort eating, without introducing a new diagnosis
Household of six includes Lilia, her partner, and other relatives on different schedules, explaining why she experiences isolation despite not living alone
optional_details: Lilia keeps a small television on in her room at night, which is often when the binge eating happens
She has a nickname for her partner, 'mi gallina clueca' (my mother hen), used affectionately when annoyed by his hovering

assigned_traits.readiness: precontemplation: does not see a reason to change
assigned_traits.eating: relies on convenience and ready meals because cooking for one feels pointless
assigned_traits.held_back: eats for comfort or in binges and is ashamed of it
assigned_traits.support: a partner who is supportive but anxious and hovers
